Use this page to understand how the router picks a model when you do not name one, and to read back the reason for any choice. How a model is chosen A request without a model is routed by the key's rules. The rules are policy data: a task class, a data class, a consequence class and a price ceiling narrow the candidates, and the router picks among those left. State the classes yourself A caller may state the classes in these headers: X-MassRelay-Task-Class X-MassRelay-Data-Class X-MassRelay-Consequence-Class Note A class the key's lane cannot enforce is refused with a 400 rather than ignored.

Use this page to learn how large a request may be and how fast you may send requests. Request size The default ceiling on a request body is 32 MiB. The plan ceiling and the route class's own limit apply too, and the smaller one wins. Over the limit is a 413. Request rate The rate limit is applied per workspace first and then per key, with a smooth (GCRA) window. A request over it is a 429 with Retry-After , and it does not wait in a queue. Use this page if you arrive from an aggregator and expect the same surface. The wire formats are the same; three things differ on purpose. The fee is a line The router never hides its fee in a price. When a request is charged a request fee it is its own line in the usage ledger, next to the model cost, and the rule is in Bring your own key . What you pay the provider and what you pay the router are never one number. Direct beats the aggregator When you bring your own provider key the router calls the provider directly with your key. The router is the distribution and the policy, not a reseller
